# Repository conventions

## No emojis, anywhere, ever

Do not write emoji characters into any file in this repository. This
applies to source code, comments, documentation, commit messages, pull
request titles and descriptions, changelog entries, and any other text
you author on behalf of this repo.

This rule overrides any default attribution footer, template, or
"generated by" line that would otherwise include an emoji. Keep the
attribution link text if the harness requires it, but strip the emoji.

A pre-commit hook in `.githooks/pre-commit` enforces this locally.
Enable it once per clone:

    git config core.hooksPath .githooks

## Testing changes

Build validation is not always possible in remote sandbox environments
because the Android Gradle plugin may be unreachable. When you cannot
run `./gradlew :TeamCode:compileDebugJavaWithJavac`, say so explicitly
in the change description rather than claiming a green build.
